subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Uber Cover-Up
description: A quick, practical guide to The Uber Cover-Up.

hook.text: Uber was hacked in 2016. Instead of reporting it, the company paid the hackers $100,000 to stay quiet.

buildup.text: Hackers stole personal data of 57 million riders and drivers, including license numbers.

discovery.text: Uber's security team paid the ransom through a bug bounty program to disguise it as a legitimate payment.

twist.text: The cover-up lasted over a year. When exposed, Uber's chief security officer was fired and later convicted.

climax.text: Uber didn't just fail to protect data. It actively hid the breach from regulators and victims.

punchline.text: Hacked, paid off the hackers, then covered it up.

quiz.question: How did Uber handle the 2016 data breach?
options: Paid the hackers $100,000 and concealed the breach for over a year
Reported it to the FBI within 24 hours
